Goddess Saraswati (separate shrine within the complex)

history.dynasty: Kalyana (Later) Chalukya; traditionally attributed to the master architect Jakanachari
history.period: Original shrine completed c. 1040 CE; expansions complete by the early 12th century
history.summary: The Trikuteshwara complex is the great Kalyana Chalukya trikuta (triple-shrine) temple of Gadag. The original east-facing shrine with its vimana was completed around 1040 CE; it was then expanded with a larger mandapa and a western sanctum, and a Saraswati shrine was added to the south, axially aligned with the main temple — the complex was likely complete by the early 12th century, and its many inscriptions help date the work. The ornate carved pillars, chiselled stone screens and figurative panels made it a celebrated model of Chalukya architecture for colonial-era scholars such as James Fergusson. NOTE: the Saraswati shrine was vandalised in the past and regular pooja is not offered there (verify current status). Sources conflict slightly on architect attribution (traditional Jakanachari credit) — documented as tradition. CSV NOTE: the CSV's 'state' column wrongly holds the town name 'Gadag' — the temple is in the state of Karnataka.

name: Trikuteshwara Temple
town_description: Gadag (Gadag-Betageri) is a town and district headquarters in north Karnataka, about 60 km from Hubballi. It is one of the great centres of Kalyana Chalukya art — some 50 temples were built in the region between 1050 and 1200 CE — with the temple cluster of Lakkundi about 13-17 km away.

travel.railway: Gadag Junction, a few kilometres from the temple, well connected to Hubballi and beyond.
travel.road: In the southern part of Gadag town, near the NH 67 corridor between Hubballi and Hampi; autos within town, and an easy day trip from Hubballi.

visitor_information.opening_hours: One travel blog gives 7:00 AM-12:30 PM and 5:00-8:30 PM — blog-sourced only, VERIFY locally before visiting.
